chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me of from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Sinan, from Ibn Miskan, from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about flea blood that may be on the garment: does that prevent him from salat (prayer)? He said: “No, even if it is much. And there is also no harm in something similar to it from nosebleed; he sprinkles water on it and does not wash it.”

And the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Rayyan, who said:

I wrote to the man asking whether the blood of bedbugs takes the same ruling as the blood of fleas, and whether it is permissible for someone to draw an analogy from the blood of bedbugs to fleas and thus perform salat (prayer) in it, and to reason similarly in such matters and act upon it. So he wrote, عليه السلام: “Salat (prayer) is permissible, and purity from it is better.”

key_terms.الثَّوْبِ: the garment or clothing in which one performs salat (prayer)
key_terms.الرُّعَافِ: nosebleed mentioned as a comparable case
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual prayer whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.الطُّهْرُ مِنْهُ أَفْضَلُ: being free of it in a state of purity is preferable
key_terms.تَجُوزُ الصَّلَاةُ: the prayer is valid and permissible
key_terms.دَمُ الْبَقِّ: the blood of bedbugs discussed in the second report
key_terms.دَمِ الْبَرَاغِيثِ: the blood of fleas found on clothing

ai.seo_question: Does flea or bedbug blood on clothing invalidate salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning small amounts of blood from fleas and bedbugs on clothing during salat (prayer). It indicates that salat remains valid with such blood, while noting that being free of it and maintaining greater taharah (ritual purity) is preferable.
